# HTTP Request Signing with HMAC-SHA256

This function builds a signature by creating a **canonical string** from the request details and signing it with **HMAC-SHA256** using your API key. A timestamp and nonce are included to prevent replay attacks.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
import time
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, parse_qsl, urlencode, quote


def sign_request(url: str, method: str, api_key: str, body: bytes = b"",
                 timestamp: int | None = None, nonce: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """
    Build an HMAC-SHA256 signature for an HTTP request.

    Args:
        url: Full request URL (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/items?b=2&a=1").
        method: HTTP method (e.g. "GET", "POST").
        api_key: Secret key used to sign the request.
        body: Optional raw request body (bytes).
        timestamp: Optional Unix timestamp (defaults to now). Useful for testing.
        nonce: Optional unique string (defaults to a random value).

    Returns:
        A dict of headers to attach to the request.
    """
    if not api_key:
        raise ValueError("api_key must be a non-empty string")
    if not method:
        raise ValueError("method must be a non-empty string")

    method = method.upper()
    timestamp = str(timestamp if timestamp is not None else int(time.time()))
    nonce = nonce or secrets.token_hex(16)

    # Normalize the URL components
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    if not parts.scheme or not parts.netloc:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid URL: {url!r}")

    host = parts.netloc.lower()
    path = quote(parts.path or "/", safe="/-_.~%")

    # Sort query parameters so ordering doesn't change the signature
    query_pairs = sorted(parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True))
    canonical_query = urlencode(query_pairs, quote_via=quote)

    # Hash the body so large payloads don't bloat the signed string
    body_hash = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()

    # Canonical string: one component per line
    canonical = "\n".join([
        method,
        host,
        path,
        canonical_query,
        timestamp,
        nonce,
        body_hash,
    ])

    signature = hmac.new(
        api_key.encode("utf-8"),
        canonical.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return {
        "X-Timestamp": timestamp,
        "X-Nonce": nonce,
        "X-Content-SHA256": body_hash,
        "X-Signature": signature,
    }


def verify_request(url: str, method: str, api_key: str, headers: dict,
                   body: bytes = b"", max_age_seconds: int = 300) -> bool:
    """Server-side check: recompute the signature and compare safely."""
    try:
        ts = int(headers["X-Timestamp"])
        nonce = headers["X-Nonce"]
        provided = headers["X-Signature"]
    except (KeyError, ValueError):
        return False

    if abs(time.time() - ts) > max_age_seconds:
        return False  # too old (or clock skew too large)

    expected = sign_request(url, method, api_key, body, timestamp=ts, nonce=nonce)
    # Constant-time comparison prevents timing attacks
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected["X-Signature"], provided)
```

## Example Usage

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    key = "my-secret-api-key"
    url = "https://api.example.com/v1/items?limit=10&sort=asc"

    headers = sign_request(url, "get", key)
    for k, v in headers.items():
        print(f"{k}: {v}")

    # Verification succeeds with the same inputs
    print("Valid:", verify_request(url, "GET", key, headers))

    # Query param order doesn't matter (canonicalized)
    reordered = "https://api.example.com/v1/items?sort=asc&limit=10"
    print("Reordered valid:", verify_request(reordered, "GET", key, headers))

    # Tampering is detected
    tampered = "https://api.example.com/v1/items?limit=1000&sort=asc"
    print("Tampered valid:", verify_request(tampered, "GET", key, headers))
```

**Sample output:**
```
X-Timestamp: 1718000000
X-Nonce: 3f9a1c...e2
X-Content-SHA256: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
X-Signature: 7d2f...a91
Valid: True
Reordered valid: True
Tampered valid: False
```

## Design Notes

| Feature | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **HMAC-SHA256** | The key never travels over the wire; only the signature does. |
| **Canonicalization** | Uppercased method, lowercased host, and sorted query params mean equivalent requests produce identical signatures. |
| **Timestamp** | Lets the server reject stale requests. |
| **Nonce** | Makes each signature unique. Store recently seen nonces server-side to fully block replays. |
| **Body hash** | Protects POST/PUT payloads from tampering. |
| **`hmac.compare_digest`** | Constant-time comparison avoids leaking info through timing. |

# HTTP Request Signing in Python

This function builds an HMAC-SHA256 signature over a canonical form of the request. It includes a timestamp and nonce to prevent replay attacks, and a body hash for integrity.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
import time
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, parse_qsl, quote


def build_request_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    api_secret: str,
    body: bytes = b"",
    timestamp: int | None = None,
    nonce: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """
    Build signature headers for an HTTP request.

    The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 over a canonical string:

        METHOD\\n
        host\\n
        /path\\n
        sorted&encoded=query\\n
        timestamp\\n
        nonce\\n
        sha256(body)

    Args:
        url:        Full request URL, e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/items?b=2&a=1".
        method:     HTTP method, e.g. "GET" or "POST".
        api_key:    Public key identifier, sent in a header.
        api_secret: Secret used for signing. It is never sent.
        body:       Raw request body bytes. Defaults to empty.
        timestamp:  Unix seconds. Defaults to now. Override for testing.
        nonce:      Unique per-request value. Defaults to a random token.

    Returns:
        A dict of headers to attach to the request.
    """
    if not api_key or not api_secret:
        raise ValueError("api_key and api_secret must be non-empty")

    method = method.upper().strip()
    if not method.isalpha():
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid HTTP method: {method!r}")

    parts = urlsplit(url)
    if parts.scheme not in ("http", "https") or not parts.hostname:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid URL: {url!r}")

    host = parts.hostname.lower()
    if parts.port and parts.port not in (80, 443):
        host = f"{host}:{parts.port}"

    path = quote(parts.path or "/", safe="/-_.~%")

    # Canonical query: decode, sort by key then value, re-encode consistently.
    query_pairs = sorted(parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True))
    canonical_query = "&".join(
        f"{quote(k, safe='-_.~')}={quote(v, safe='-_.~')}" for k, v in query_pairs
    )

    ts = str(int(time.time()) if timestamp is None else int(timestamp))
    nonce = nonce or secrets.token_hex(16)
    body_hash = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()

    string_to_sign = "\n".join(
        [method, host, path, canonical_query, ts, nonce, body_hash]
    )

    signature = hmac.new(
        api_secret.encode("utf-8"),
        string_to_sign.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return {
        "X-Api-Key": api_key,
        "X-Timestamp": ts,
        "X-Nonce": nonce,
        "X-Content-SHA256": body_hash,
        "X-Signature": signature,
    }


def verify_request_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    headers: dict[str, str],
    api_secret: str,
    body: bytes = b"",
    max_skew_seconds: int = 300,
) -> bool:
    """Server-side check: recompute the signature and compare in constant time."""
    try:
        ts = int(headers["X-Timestamp"])
        if abs(time.time() - ts) > max_skew_seconds:
            return False
        expected = build_request_signature(
            url, method, headers["X-Api-Key"], api_secret,
            body=body, timestamp=ts, nonce=headers["X-Nonce"],
        )
    except (KeyError, ValueError):
        return False
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected["X-Signature"], headers.get("X-Signature", ""))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    secret = "s3cr3t-do-not-share"
    url = "https://api.example.com/v1/items?limit=10&sort=name"
    body = b'{"name": "widget"}'

    hdrs = build_request_signature(url, "post", "my-key-id", secret, body=body)
    for k, v in hdrs.items():
        print(f"{k}: {v}")

    print("valid:", verify_request_signature(url, "POST", hdrs, secret, body=body))
    print("tampered:", verify_request_signature(url, "POST", hdrs, secret, body=b"{}"))
```

## Design Notes

- **Key versus secret:** The `api_key` identifies the client and is sent in a header. The `api_secret` signs the request and is never transmitted. If you only have a single key, pass it as `api_secret` and use a separate client ID for `api_key`.
- **Canonicalization:** The method is uppercased, the host is lowercased, and query parameters are sorted and re-encoded. Equivalent requests therefore produce the same signature regardless of parameter order.
- **Replay protection:** The timestamp limits how long a signature stays valid. The nonce lets the server reject duplicates. To fully block replays, store seen nonces for the skew window.
- **Integrity:** The body hash means any change to the payload invalidates the signature.
- **Constant-time comparison:** `hmac.compare_digest` avoids timing attacks during verification.

Usage with `requests`:

```python
import requests
headers = build_request_signature(url, "POST", key, secret, body=body)
requests.post(url, data=body, headers={**headers, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
```

Make sure you send exactly the same `body` bytes that you signed.

# HMAC-SHA256 Request Signing in Python

Below is a request signer that builds a canonical string from the request, signs it with HMAC-SHA256, and returns headers you can attach to the request. It also includes a matching server-side verifier.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
import time
from typing import Optional
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, parse_qsl, quote


def _canonical_query(query: str) -> str:
    """Sort query params and percent-encode them consistently."""
    pairs = parse_qsl(query, keep_blank_values=True)
    pairs.sort()
    return "&".join(
        f"{quote(k, safe='-_.~')}={quote(v, safe='-_.~')}" for k, v in pairs
    )


def build_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    body: bytes = b"",
    timestamp: Optional[int] = None,
    nonce: Optional[str] = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Build HMAC-SHA256 signature headers for an HTTP request.

    Args:
        url:       Full request URL (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/items?b=2&a=1").
        method:    HTTP method (e.g. "GET", "POST").
        api_key:   Shared secret key used to sign the request.
        body:      Raw request body bytes (empty for GET).
        timestamp: Unix time in seconds (defaults to now).
        nonce:     Unique random value (defaults to a new random token).

    Returns:
        A dict of headers to attach to the request.
    """
    if not api_key:
        raise ValueError("api_key must be non-empty")
    if not method:
        raise ValueError("method must be non-empty")

    parts = urlsplit(url)
    if not parts.scheme or not parts.netloc:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid URL: {url!r}")

    timestamp = int(time.time()) if timestamp is None else int(timestamp)
    nonce = nonce or secrets.token_hex(16)
    body_hash = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()

    canonical = "\n".join([
        method.upper(),
        parts.netloc.lower(),
        parts.path or "/",
        _canonical_query(parts.query),
        str(timestamp),
        nonce,
        body_hash,
    ])

    signature = hmac.new(
        api_key.encode("utf-8"),
        canonical.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return {
        "X-Timestamp": str(timestamp),
        "X-Nonce": nonce,
        "X-Content-SHA256": body_hash,
        "X-Signature": signature,
    }


def verify_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    headers: dict,
    body: bytes = b"",
    max_skew_seconds: int = 300,
) -> bool:
    """Server-side check: recompute the signature and compare in constant time."""
    try:
        ts = int(headers["X-Timestamp"])
        nonce = headers["X-Nonce"]
        provided = headers["X-Signature"]
    except (KeyError, ValueError):
        return False

    if abs(time.time() - ts) > max_skew_seconds:
        return False  # stale or future-dated request

    expected = build_signature(url, method, api_key, body, ts, nonce)["X-Signature"]
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, provided)
```

## Example usage

```python
import json

api_key = "my-secret-api-key"
url = "https://api.example.com/v1/orders?limit=10&sort=desc"
body = json.dumps({"item": "widget", "qty": 3}).encode()

headers = build_signature(url, "POST", api_key, body)
print(headers)
# {'X-Timestamp': '1717000000', 'X-Nonce': '9f2c...', 'X-Content-SHA256': '...', 'X-Signature': '...'}

# Server side
print(verify_signature(url, "POST", api_key, headers, body))         # True
print(verify_signature(url, "POST", api_key, headers, b"tampered"))  # False
```

With `requests`:

```python
import requests
requests.post(url, data=body, headers={**headers, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
```

## Design notes

- **HMAC, not a plain hash.** `sha256(key + message)` is vulnerable to length-extension attacks. HMAC is the correct construction.
- **Canonicalization.** Query parameters are sorted and encoded consistently, so `?b=2&a=1` and `?a=1&b=2` produce the same signature on both sides.
- **Timestamp and nonce.** These limit replay attacks. The server rejects old timestamps and should also remember recently seen nonces (e.g., in Redis with a TTL equal to `max_skew_seconds`).
- **Body hash.** Including the body hash prevents payload tampering.
- **Constant-time comparison.** `hmac.compare_digest` avoids timing side channels during verification.
- **Never send the key itself.** Only the signature travels over the wire. If you need to identify the client, add a separate public key ID header (e.g., `X-Key-Id`).

5. **Constant-time comparison**: `hmac.compare_digest` prevents timing attacks during verification.

- **Key vs. secret**: An "API key" alone shouldn't be used as the HMAC secret if it's ever transmitted. That's why the function takes a public `api_key` plus a private `api_secret`. If your system only has one value, pass it as `api_secret` and use an identifier for `api_key`.
- **Nonce tracking**: For full replay protection, the server should store nonces (e.g., in Redis with a TTL equal to `max_skew_seconds`) and reject duplicates.
- **Use with `requests`**: You can attach the headers directly:
  ```python
  requests.post(url, data=body, headers=sign_request(url, "POST", key, secret, body))
  ```

# HTTP Request Signature Builder

This function creates an HMAC-SHA256 signature over a canonical form of the request. It includes a timestamp and nonce to protect against replay attacks.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
import time
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, parse_qsl, urlencode, quote


def build_request_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    body: bytes = b"",
    timestamp: int | None = None,
    nonce: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """
    Build an HMAC-SHA256 signature for an HTTP request.

    Args:
        url:       Full request URL (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/items?b=2&a=1").
        method:    HTTP method (e.g. "GET", "POST").
        api_key:   Secret key used to sign the request.
        body:      Raw request body (optional; empty for GET).
        timestamp: Unix timestamp in seconds (defaults to now).
        nonce:     Unique random value (defaults to a random 16-byte hex string).

    Returns:
        A dict of headers to attach to the request.
    """
    if not api_key:
        raise ValueError("api_key must be a non-empty string")
    if not method:
        raise ValueError("method must be a non-empty string")

    method = method.upper()
    timestamp = int(time.time()) if timestamp is None else int(timestamp)
    nonce = nonce or secrets.token_hex(16)

    # --- Canonicalize the URL ---
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    if not parts.scheme or not parts.netloc:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid absolute URL: {url!r}")

    host = parts.netloc.lower()
    path = quote(parts.path or "/", safe="/-_.~%")
    # Sort query params so the same logical request always signs identically
    query = urlencode(sorted(parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)))

    # --- Hash the body ---
    body_hash = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()

    # --- Build the string to sign ---
    string_to_sign = "\n".join([
        method,
        host,
        path,
        query,
        str(timestamp),
        nonce,
        body_hash,
    ])

    signature = hmac.new(
        api_key.encode("utf-8"),
        string_to_sign.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return {
        "X-Timestamp": str(timestamp),
        "X-Nonce": nonce,
        "X-Content-SHA256": body_hash,
        "X-Signature": signature,
    }


def verify_request_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    headers: dict[str, str],
    body: bytes = b"",
    max_age_seconds: int = 300,
) -> bool:
    """Server-side check: recompute the signature and compare in constant time."""
    try:
        ts = int(headers["X-Timestamp"])
        nonce = headers["X-Nonce"]
        provided = headers["X-Signature"]
    except (KeyError, ValueError):
        return False

    if abs(time.time() - ts) > max_age_seconds:
        return False  # too old or too far in the future

    expected = build_request_signature(url, method, api_key, body, ts, nonce)
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected["X-Signature"], provided)
```

## Example Usage

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    key = "my-secret-api-key"

    headers = build_request_signature(
        url="https://api.example.com/v1/items?b=2&a=1",
        method="get",
        api_key=key,
    )
    for k, v in headers.items():
        print(f"{k}: {v}")

    # Verification (e.g., on the server)
    ok = verify_request_signature(
        "https://api.example.com/v1/items?a=1&b=2",  # param order doesn't matter
        "GET",
        key,
        headers,
    )
    print("Valid:", ok)  # True
```

Sample output:
```
X-Timestamp: 1718035200
X-Nonce: 3f9c1a7e0b2d4c6e8a1f0e9d7c5b3a21
X-Content-SHA256: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
X-Signature: 9a4e...c71b
Valid: True
```

## Design Notes

| Element | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **HMAC-SHA256** | Proves the sender knows the key without transmitting it. |
| **Sorted query params** | Makes `?a=1&b=2` and `?b=2&a=1` produce the same signature. |
| **Timestamp** | Lets the server reject stale requests. |
| **Nonce** | Lets the server reject replayed requests. Store recently seen nonces to enforce this. |
| **Body hash** | Prevents tampering with the POST/PUT payload. |
| **`hmac.compare_digest`** | Constant-time comparison avoids timing attacks. |

**Tip:** In production, use a separate public **key ID** (sent in a header like `X-Key-Id`) and a private **secret** (used only for signing). Never send the signing secret itself over the wire.

# HTTP Request Signing with HMAC-SHA256

The function below builds a signature from the HTTP method, a normalized URL, a timestamp, and a nonce, using HMAC-SHA256 keyed with your API key/secret. A matching verification function is included so the server side can check signatures safely.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
import time
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, parse_qsl, urlencode, quote


def _canonicalize_url(url: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    """Normalize a URL into (host, path, sorted_query) so equivalent
    URLs always produce the same signature."""
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    host = parts.hostname.lower() if parts.hostname else ""
    if parts.port and parts.port not in (80, 443):
        host = f"{host}:{parts.port}"

    path = quote(parts.path or "/", safe="/-_.~%")

    # Sort query params by key, then value, so ordering doesn't matter
    query_pairs = sorted(parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True))
    query = urlencode(query_pairs, quote_via=quote)

    return host, path, query


def sign_request(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    timestamp: int | None = None,
    nonce: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """
    Build an HMAC-SHA256 signature for an HTTP request.

    Returns a dict of headers to attach to the request:
        X-Timestamp, X-Nonce, X-Signature
    """
    if not api_key:
        raise ValueError("api_key must be a non-empty string")
    if not method:
        raise ValueError("method must be a non-empty string")

    method = method.upper()
    timestamp = int(time.time()) if timestamp is None else int(timestamp)
    nonce = nonce or secrets.token_hex(16)

    host, path, query = _canonicalize_url(url)

    # Canonical string: one field per line, fixed order
    string_to_sign = "\n".join([
        method,
        host,
        path,
        query,
        str(timestamp),
        nonce,
    ])

    signature = hmac.new(
        api_key.encode("utf-8"),
        string_to_sign.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return {
        "X-Timestamp": str(timestamp),
        "X-Nonce": nonce,
        "X-Signature": signature,
    }


def verify_request(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    headers: dict[str, str],
    max_age_seconds: int = 300,
) -> bool:
    """
    Verify a signed request. Rejects stale timestamps and uses a
    constant-time comparison to avoid timing attacks.
    (For full replay protection, also store seen nonces until they expire.)
    """
    try:
        timestamp = int(headers["X-Timestamp"])
        nonce = headers["X-Nonce"]
        provided_sig = headers["X-Signature"]
    except (KeyError, ValueError):
        return False

    if abs(time.time() - timestamp) > max_age_seconds:
        return False

    expected = sign_request(url, method, api_key, timestamp=timestamp, nonce=nonce)
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected["X-Signature"], provided_sig)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    key = "my-secret-api-key"
    url = "https://api.example.com/v1/orders?limit=10&status=open"

    headers = sign_request(url, "get", key)
    print("Headers:", headers)

    # Query parameter order doesn't affect validity
    reordered = "https://API.example.com/v1/orders?status=open&limit=10"
    print("Valid:", verify_request(reordered, "GET", key, headers))

    # Tampering is detected
    tampered = "https://api.example.com/v1/orders?limit=1000&status=open"
    print("Tampered valid:", verify_request(tampered, "GET", key, headers))
```

**Example output:**
```
Headers: {'X-Timestamp': '1718049600', 'X-Nonce': '3f9c...', 'X-Signature': 'a71b...'}
Valid: True
Tampered valid: False
```

## Design notes

- **HMAC, not plain hashing**: `sha256(key + message)` is vulnerable to length-extension attacks. HMAC avoids this.
- **Canonicalization**: Lowercasing the host, sorting query params, and normalizing the path ensure that equivalent URLs produce identical signatures on client and server.
- **Timestamp + nonce**: The timestamp limits how long a captured request stays usable. The nonce makes each signature unique. To fully block replays, the server should store recently seen nonces.
- **Constant-time comparison**: `hmac.compare_digest` prevents attackers from guessing the signature byte-by-byte through timing differences.
- **Extending it**: For POST/PUT requests, add `hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()` as another line in `string_to_sign` so the payload is covered too.
- **Key handling**: Treat the API key as a secret. It's used to *sign* and should never be sent in the request itself. Send a separate public key ID if the server needs to look up which secret to use.

Here's a function that normalizes names, handling whitespace, casing, and common name patterns like hyphens, apostrophes, and prefixes such as "Mc" and "van".

```python
import re

# Particles that are conventionally lowercase when not the first word
LOWERCASE_PARTICLES = {"van", "von", "der", "den", "de", "del", "della", "di", "da", "la", "le", "du", "bin", "al"}

SUFFIXES = {"jr": "Jr.", "sr": "Sr.", "ii": "II", "iii": "III", "iv": "IV"}


def _capitalize_word(word: str, is_first: bool) -> str:
    lower = word.lower()

    # Suffixes like Jr, III
    stripped = lower.rstrip(".")
    if not is_first and stripped in SUFFIXES:
        return SUFFIXES[stripped]

    # Lowercase particles (van, de, ...) unless at the start
    if not is_first and lower in LOWERCASE_PARTICLES:
        return lower

    # Handle hyphenated parts and apostrophes: "o'brien" -> "O'Brien"
    def cap_segment(seg: str) -> str:
        if not seg:
            return seg
        result = seg[0].upper() + seg[1:].lower()
        # Mc prefix: "mcdonald" -> "McDonald"
        if re.match(r"^Mc[a-z]", result):
            result = "Mc" + result[2].upper() + result[3:]
        return result

    parts = re.split(r"([-'’])", lower)  # keep delimiters
    return "".join(p if p in "-'’" else cap_segment(p) for p in parts)


def _normalize_part(text: str) -> str:
    words = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text.strip()).split(" ")
    words = [w for w in words if w]
    return " ".join(_capitalize_word(w, i == 0) for i, w in enumerate(words))


def normalize_display_name(first_name: str, last_name: str) -> str:
    """Return a normalized 'First Last' display name.

    >>> normalize_display_name("  jOHN ", "SMITH")
    'John Smith'
    >>> normalize_display_name("mary-jane", "o'brien")
    'Mary-Jane O'Brien'
    >>> normalize_display_name("ludwig", "van beethoven")
    'Ludwig van Beethoven'
    >>> normalize_display_name("ronald", "mcdonald jr")
    'Ronald McDonald Jr.'
    >>> normalize_display_name("", "Cher")
    'Cher'
    """
    first = _normalize_part(first_name or "")
    last = _normalize_part(last_name or "")
    return " ".join(p for p in (first, last) if p)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import doctest
    doctest.testmod()
```

**What it does:**
- Trims leading/trailing whitespace and collapses internal runs of whitespace.
- Converts to proper capitalization regardless of input case.
- Handles hyphenated names (`mary-jane` → `Mary-Jane`) and apostrophes (`o'brien` → `O'Brien`).
- Handles `Mc` prefixes and suffixes (`Jr.`, `III`).
- Keeps particles like `van` and `de` lowercase in the middle of a name.
- Works if either name is empty or `None`.

**Caveats:** Name capitalization is culturally varied, so no rule set is perfect. For example, `MacDonald`, `DeShawn`, and `van` capitalized in some families can't be inferred automatically. If you're handling user-entered names, consider preserving the user's original input when it's mixed-case, and only normalizing when it's all upper or all lower.

```python
            piece = "'".join(apos_parts)

            if re.match(r"^Mc[a-z]{2,}", piece):

            hyphen_parts.append(piece)
```

runs.prompt: Write a Python function that builds a small HTTP request signature from a URL, a method, and an API key.
runs.output:
This sketch builds an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the method, the URL path and query, a timestamp, and a nonce. The server can recompute it with the shared secret and compare.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
import time
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, parse_qsl, urlencode


def sign_request(url: str, method: str, api_key: str, secret: str,
                 timestamp: int | None = None, nonce: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """
    Build a small HMAC-SHA256 signature for an HTTP request.

    Returns headers to attach to the request.
    """
    method = method.upper()
    timestamp = timestamp if timestamp is not None else int(time.time())
    nonce = nonce or secrets.token_hex(8)

    parts = urlsplit(url)
    path = parts.path or "/"

    # Sort query params so the same logical URL always yields the same string
    query = urlencode(sorted(parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)))

    # Canonical string: each field on its own line
    string_to_sign = "\n".join([
        method,
        parts.netloc.lower(),
        path,
        query,
        str(timestamp),
        nonce,
    ])

    signature = hmac.new(
        secret.encode("utf-8"),
        string_to_sign.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return {
        "X-Api-Key": api_key,
        "X-Timestamp": str(timestamp),
        "X-Nonce": nonce,
        "X-Signature": signature,
    }


def verify_request(url, method, api_key, secret, headers, max_age=300) -> bool:
    """Server-side check: recompute and compare in constant time."""
    try:
        ts = int(headers["X-Timestamp"])
        if abs(time.time() - ts) > max_age:
            return False  # too old or from the future
        expected = sign_request(url, method, api_key, secret,
                                timestamp=ts, nonce=headers["X-Nonce"])
        return hmac.compare_digest(expected["X-Signature"], headers["X-Signature"])
    except (KeyError, ValueError):
        return False


if __name__ == "__main__":
    headers = sign_request(
        "https://api.example.com/v1/items?b=2&a=1",
        "get",
        api_key="my-key-id",
        secret="my-shared-secret",
    )
    print(headers)
```

**Design notes**

- **API key vs. secret:** The API key is a public identifier sent in a header. The secret is never transmitted and is used only to compute the HMAC. If you only have one value, you can use it as the secret, but then the "key" shouldn't also be sent in plaintext.
- **Canonicalization:** Uppercasing the method, lowercasing the host, and sorting query parameters means both sides build identical strings.
- **Replay protection:** The timestamp and nonce let the server reject old requests. To be fully effective, the server should also remember recently seen nonces.
- **Constant-time comparison:** `hmac.compare_digest` avoids timing attacks.
- **Body:** For POST/PUT requests, add a hash of the body (e.g., `hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()`) as another line in `string_to_sign`, so the payload is covered too.

# Normalized Display Name

```python
def normalize_name(first_name: str, last_name: str) -> str:
    """
    Normalize a first and last name into a display name.

    - Strips leading/trailing whitespace
    - Collapses internal whitespace
    - Capitalizes each word (title case)

    Examples:
        >>> normalize_name("  john ", "DOE  ")
        'John Doe'
        >>> normalize_name("mary-jane", "watson")
        'Mary-Jane Watson'
    """
    full_name = " ".join([first_name.strip(), last_name.strip()])
    # Collapse multiple spaces between words
    full_name = " ".join(full_name.split())
    # Title-case each word, preserving hyphenated names
    return " ".join(word.capitalize() for word in full_name.split(" "))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(normalize_name("  john ", "DOE"))       # John Doe
    print(normalize_name("mary-jane", "watson"))  # Mary-Jane Watson
    print(normalize_name("", "smith"))            # Smith
```

**Notes:**
- `str.capitalize()` handles hyphenated names better than `str.title()` (which would turn "Mary-Jane" into "Mary-Jane" but "O'brien" into "O'Brien" incorrectly).
- If a name part is empty, it's simply skipped due to the whitespace collapsing, so you won't get double spaces.
- For stricter handling of names like "McDonald" or "van der Berg," you'd need a name-aware casing library (e.g., a list of exceptions), since automatic capitalization can't know cultural capitalization rules.

Here's a function that normalizes names for display:

```python
def normalize_name(first_name, last_name):
    """
    Takes a first name and last name and returns a normalized display name.

    - Strips whitespace
    - Capitalizes each part properly (handles lowercase, uppercase, mixed case)
    - Handles empty parts gracefully
    - Returns "Unknown" if both names are missing
    """
    first = (first_name or "").strip().title()
    last = (last_name or "").strip().title()

    parts = [p for p in (first, last) if p]

    if not parts:
        return "Unknown"

    return " ".join(parts)
```

Here's a clean, compact implementation using HMAC (the standard way to sign requests):

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
from urllib.parse import urlparse


def sign_request(method: str, url: str, api_key: str) -> str:
    """Build a short signature string for an HTTP request.

    Format: METHOD:HOST:PATH:HEX_DIGEST
    """
    # Normalize inputs
    method = method.upper()
    key = api_key.encode("utf-8")

    # Break down the URL into stable parts
    parsed = urlparse(url)
    host = parsed.netloc.lower()
    path = parsed.path or "/"

    # Message to sign: method + host + path
    message = f"{method}\n{host}\n{path}".encode("utf-8")

    # HMAC-SHA256, truncated to keep the signature small
    digest = hmac.new(key, message, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()[:16]

    return f"{method}:{host}:{path}:{digest}"
```

Example usage:

```python
sig = sign_request("GET", "https://api.example.com/v1/users", "my-secret-key")
print(sig)
# GET:api.example.com:/v1/users:3fa2b9c1d84e07f6
```

**Why this design:**

- **HMAC-SHA256** is the industry standard — it's keyed, so only someone with the same `api_key` can reproduce the signature.
- **Truncating to 16 hex chars** (64 bits) keeps it "small" while still being collision-resistant for this use case. Drop the truncation if you need full security strength.
- **Including method, host, and path** in the signed message means the signature is invalidated if any of them are tampered with.
- The function is pure (no side effects), making it easy to test.

**Optional extension:** if you also want query parameters or headers signed, just append them to the `message` string in a defined order (e.g., sorted by key) — a common pattern in APIs like AWS Signature Version 4.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac

def build_signature(url: str, method: str, api_key: str) -> str:
    """

    Args:
        url:     Full URL, e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users?b=2&a=1"

    # regardless of parameter order.
    sorted_query = urlencode(sorted(parse_qsl(parts.query)))

    message = "\n".join([
        method.upper(),
        parts.path or "/",
        sorted_query,
    ])

    signature = hmac.new(
        api_key.encode("utf-8"),
        message.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return signature
```

```python
"""Helpers for turning raw name fields into a clean, normalized display name."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata

_WHITESPACE_RE = re.compile(r"\s+")


def _clean(value: str | None) -> str:
    """Strip control chars, normalize unicode, and collapse whitespace."""
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError(f"expected str or None, got {type(value).__name__}")

    value = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", value)          # full-width -> ASCII, composed accents
    value = "".join(ch for ch in value if ch.isprintable())  # drop \n, \t, zero-width, etc.
    return _WHITESPACE_RE.sub(" ", value).strip()


def _cap_chunk(chunk: str) -> str:
    """Capitalize a chunk, keeping apostrophe-led names like O'Brien intact."""
    out: list[str] = []
    capitalize_next = True
    for ch in chunk:
        if capitalize_next and ch.isalpha():
            out.append(ch.upper())
            capitalize_next = False
        else:
            out.append(ch.lower())
            if ch == "'":
                capitalize_next = True
    return "".join(out)


def _titlecase_part(part: str) -> str:
    """Title-case each word, treating hyphens as internal boundaries."""
    if not part:
        return ""
    words = ["-".join(_cap_chunk(c) for c in word.split("-")) for word in part.split(" ")]
    return " ".join(words)


def normalize_display_name(
    first_name: str | None,
    last_name: str | None = None,
    *,
    separator: str = " ",
    case: str = "title",
) -> str:
    """Return a normalized display name built from a first and last name.

    Args:
        first_name: Given name. May be None or empty.
        last_name: Family name. May be None or empty.
        separator: String placed between the two parts.
        case: "title" (default), "upper", "lower", or "preserve".

    Returns:
        The combined display name, with empty parts omitted.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If a name is not a string or None.
        ValueError: If `case` is not one of the supported values.
    """
    if case not in {"title", "upper", "lower", "preserve"}:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported case: {case!r}")

    first = _clean(first_name)
    last = _clean(last_name)

    if case == "title":
        first, last = _titlecase_part(first), _titlecase_part(last)
    elif case == "upper":
        first, last = first.upper(), last.upper()
    elif case == "lower":
        first, last = first.lower(), last.lower()

    return separator.join(part for part in (first, last) if part)
```

```python
normalize_display_name("jane", "o'brien")          # 'Jane O'Brien'

normalize_display_name("JOHN", "SMITH", case="upper")  # 'JOHN SMITH'
normalize_display_name("John", None)              # 'John'
normalize_display_name("", "")                   # ''
normalize_display_name("John", "Smith", separator=", ")  # 'John, Smith'
```

- **Non-Latin scripts** are left alone by the title-caser (it only touches `isalpha()` characters), so `李雷` passes through unchanged.

```python
    first, last = _clean(first_name), _clean(last_name)
```

"Normalized" is ambiguous, so here are the rules I implemented (all easy to change):

- Collapse extra whitespace, strip leading/trailing spaces, normalize Unicode (NFC).
- Title-case each word, but keep **name particles** lowercase (`van`, `de`, `von`, `della`, …) unless they're the very first token of the whole name → `Ludwig van Beethoven`.
- Handle `Mc`/`Mac` prefixes → `McDonald`, `MacArthur`.
- Handle hyphens and apostrophes → `Smith-Jones`, `O'Brien`.
- Curly apostrophes (`’`) are converted to straight ones.
- Optional accent stripping (`José` → `Jose`) and an optional `Last, First` output style.

```python
"""Build a normalized display name from a first name and last name."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata

__all__ = ["normalize_display_name"]

# Particles that stay lowercase when they appear inside a name.
_PARTICLES = frozenset({
    "al", "bin", "da", "de", "del", "della", "der", "di", "do", "dos", "du",
    "e", "el", "i", "ibn", "la", "le", "lo", "los", "ten", "ter", "van",
    "von", "y",
})

_APOSTROPHES = {"\u2019": "'", "\u02bc": "'", "\u2018": "'"}
_SEPARATORS = re.compile(r"([-'])")


def _clean(text: str, field: str) -> str:
    """Validate and normalize whitespace/unicode for one name field."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise TypeError(f"{field} must be a str, got {type(text).__name__}")

    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", text)
    for src, dst in _APOSTROPHES.items():
        text = text.replace(src, dst)
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()

    if not text:
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must not be empty")
    return text


def _title_word(word: str, *, first: bool) -> str:
    """Title-case a single word, honoring particles and Mc/Mac prefixes."""
    low = word.lower()

    if not first and low in _PARTICLES:
        return low

    # McDonald / MacArthur style prefixes.
    for prefix in ("mac", "mc"):
        if low.startswith(prefix) and len(low) - len(prefix) >= 3:
            rest = low[len(prefix):]
            return prefix.capitalize() + rest[:1].upper() + rest[1:]

    # Capitalize each part around hyphens and apostrophes.
    return "".join(
        part if part in "-'" else part[:1].upper() + part[1:].lower()
        for part in _SEPARATORS.split(word)
    )


def _strip_accents(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove diacritics: 'José' -> 'Jose'."""
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", text)
    return "".join(c for c in decomposed if not unicodedata.combining(c))


def normalize_display_name(
    first_name: str,
    last_name: str,
    *,
    style: str = "first_last",
    strip_accents: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Return a normalized display name built from *first_name* and *last_name*.

    Args:
        first_name: Given name, e.g. "  ludwig " or "MARIE-CLAIRE".
        last_name: Family name; may contain particles, e.g. "van beethoven".
        style: "first_last" (default) -> "Ludwig van Beethoven";
               "last_first" -> "van Beethoven, Ludwig".
        strip_accents: If True, drop diacritics ("José" -> "Jose").

    Returns:
        The normalized display name.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If either argument is not a string.
        ValueError: If either argument is empty/whitespace-only, or *style*
            is unknown.
    """
    if style not in {"first_last", "last_first"}:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown style: {style!r}")

    first_tokens = _clean(first_name, "first_name").split(" ")
    last_tokens = _clean(last_name, "last_name").split(" ")

    ordered = (
        first_tokens + last_tokens
        if style == "first_last"
        else last_tokens + first_tokens
    )

    rendered = [
        _title_word(token, first=(index == 0))
        for index, token in enumerate(ordered)
    ]

    if style == "last_first":
        split = len(last_tokens)
        name = " ".join(rendered[:split]) + ", " + " ".join(rendered[split:])
    else:
        name = " ".join(rendered)

    return _strip_accents(name) if strip_accents else name
```

```python
normalize_display_name("MARIE-CLAIRE", "SMITH-JONES")  # 'Marie-Claire Smith-Jones'
normalize_display_name("shaun", "o'brien")             # "Shaun O'Brien"
normalize_display_name("angela", "mcdonald")          # 'Angela McDonald'

normalize_display_name("ludwig", "van beethoven", style="last_first")
# 'van Beethoven, Ludwig'
```

- **Trim & collapse** whitespace; strip stray punctuation (commas, quotes, trailing periods)
- **Consistent casing** — title case by default, with correct handling of apostrophes (`o'brien` → `O'Brien`) and hyphens (`jean-luc` → `Jean-Luc`)
- **Optional accent folding** (`josé` → `Jose`) for systems that can't store non-ASCII
- **Graceful degradation** — missing last name → `"Ada"`; missing first name → `"Lovelace"`
- **Several output styles** — `"First Last"`, `"Last, First"`, or `"A. Lovelace"`

```python
"""Helpers for building normalized display names."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata

__all__ = ["normalize_display_name", "normalize_sort_key"]

_WHITESPACE_RE = re.compile(r"\s+")
# Keep letters (any script), digits, spaces, apostrophes, hyphens, periods.
_DISALLOWED_RE = re.compile(r"[^0-9A-Za-z\sÀ-ɏ'’\-.]")
_APOSTROPHES = "'’"


def _clean(raw: str, *, strip_accents: bool) -> str:
    """Remove unwanted characters and normalize whitespace."""
    if strip_accents:
        raw = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", raw)
        raw = "".join(ch for ch in raw if not unicodedata.combining(ch))
    raw = _DISALLOWED_RE.sub(" ", raw)
    raw = _WHITESPACE_RE.sub(" ", raw).strip()
    return raw.strip(" .,-")


def _titlecase_word(word: str) -> str:
    """Title-case a single word, respecting apostrophes and hyphens."""
    hyphenated = []
    for chunk in word.split("-"):
        out, capitalize_next = [], True
        for segment in re.split(f"([{_APOSTROPHES}])", chunk):
            if segment in ("'", "’"):
                out.append(segment)
                capitalize_next = True
            elif segment:
                out.append(segment.capitalize() if capitalize_next else segment.lower())
                capitalize_next = False
        hyphenated.append("".join(out))
    return "-".join(hyphenated)


def _apply_case(text: str, case: str) -> str:
    if case == "title":
        return " ".join(_titlecase_word(w) for w in text.split())
    if case == "upper":
        return text.upper()
    if case == "lower":
        return text.lower()
    if case == "keep":
        return text
    raise ValueError(f"unknown case option: {case!r}")


def normalize_display_name(
    first_name: str | None,
    last_name: str | None,
    *,
    style: str = "first_last",
    case: str = "title",
    strip_accents: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Return a normalized display name built from a first and last name.

    Args:
        first_name: Given name; may be None or empty.
        last_name: Family name; may be None or empty.
        style: "first_last" -> "Ada Lovelace"
               "last_first" -> "Lovelace, Ada"
               "initials"   -> "A. Lovelace"
        case: "title" (default), "upper", "lower", or "keep".
        strip_accents: Fold accented characters to ASCII (e.g. "José" -> "Jose").

    Returns:
        The formatted display name.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If a name argument is not a string or None.
        ValueError: If both names are empty, or style/case is invalid.
    """
    for label, value in (("first_name", first_name), ("last_name", last_name)):
        if value is not None and not isinstance(value, str):
            raise TypeError(f"{label} must be a string or None, got {type(value).__name__}")

    first = _clean(first_name or "", strip_accents=strip_accents)
    last = _clean(last_name or "", strip_accents=strip_accents)

    if not first and not last:
        raise ValueError("at least one of first_name or last_name must be non-empty")

    first = _apply_case(first, case)
    last = _apply_case(last, case)

    if style == "first_last":
        return " ".join(p for p in (first, last) if p)
    if style == "last_first":
        if first and last:
            return f"{last}, {first}"
        return first or last
    if style == "initials":
        initial = f"{first[0]}." if first else ""
        return " ".join(p for p in (initial, last) if p)
    raise ValueError(f"unknown style option: {style!r}")


def normalize_sort_key(first_name: str | None, last_name: str | None) -> str:
    """Return a lowercase 'last, first' key suitable for sorting or indexing."""
    display = normalize_display_name(first_name, last_name, style="last_first", case="lower")
    return display
```

```python
# 'Ada Lovelace'

normalize_display_name("jean-luc", "o'brien")
# 'Jean-Luc O'Brien'

normalize_display_name("Ada", "")
# 'Ada'

normalize_display_name("Ada", "Lovelace", style="last_first")
# 'Lovelace, Ada'
```

Here's a robust version that handles whitespace, Unicode, punctuation, and name casing:

```python
import re
import unicodedata

_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")
_ILLEGAL = re.compile(r"[^\w\s'’-]", re.UNICODE)

# Particles that stay lowercase when they aren't the first word of a name
_PARTICLES = {
    "van", "von", "de", "del", "della", "der", "den", "di", "da", "do", "dos",
    "du", "la", "le", "lo", "bin", "ibn", "al", "el", "mac", "mc", "st",
}


def _clean(part: str | None) -> str:
    """Strip and tidy a single name component."""
    if not part:
        return ""
    # Normalize compatibility forms (e.g. full-width, composed accents)
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", part)
    # Collapse internal whitespace and trim
    text = _WHITESPACE.sub(" ", text).strip()
    # Drop characters that don't belong in names (digits, punctuation, emoji)
    text = _ILLEGAL.sub("", text)
    return _WHITESPACE.sub(" ", text).strip()


def _title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Capitalize words and letters after hyphens/apostrophes; keep particles lower."""
    words = []
    for i, word in enumerate(text.split(" ")):
        if not word:
            continue
        if i > 0 and word.lower() in _PARTICLES:
            words.append(word.lower())
            continue
        # Capitalize the first letter of each "sub-word" (handles O'Brien, Smith-Jones)
        out = []
        capitalize_next = True
        for ch in word:
            if capitalize_next:
                out.append(ch.upper())
                capitalize_next = False
            else:
                out.append(ch)
            if ch in "-'":
                capitalize_next = True
        words.append("".join(out))
    return " ".join(words)


def normalize_display_name(first_name: str | None,
                           last_name: str | None,
                           case: str = "title") -> str:
    """
    Return a normalized display name of the form "First Last".

    - Whitespace is collapsed and trimmed; empty components are omitted.
    - Unicode is normalized (NFKC) and stray punctuation is removed.
    - `case` may be "title" (default), "upper", "lower", or "keep".
    - Raises ValueError if both names are empty.
    """
    first = _clean(first_name)
    last = _clean(last_name)

    if not first and not last:
        raise ValueError("At least one of first_name or last_name is required")

    parts = [p for p in (first, last) if p]

    if case == "title":
        parts = [_title_case(p) for p in parts]
    elif case == "upper":
        parts = [p.upper() for p in parts]
    elif case == "lower":
        parts = [p.lower() for p in parts]
    elif case != "keep":
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown case option: {case!r}")

    return " ".join(parts)
```

**Examples**

```python
normalize_display_name("  john ", "de la cruz")   # 'John de la Cruz'
normalize_display_name("o'brien", "mcdonald-smith") # "O'Brien McDonald-Smith"
normalize_display_name("élodie", "dupont")          # 'Élodie Dupont'
normalize_display_name("jane", None)                # 'Jane'
normalize_display_name("", "  ")                    # raises ValueError
normalize_display_name("john", "doe", case="upper") # 'JOHN DOE'
```

A few design notes:
- **Casing** capitalizes the first letter of each word and after hyphens/apostrophes, but leaves the rest of the letters alone — so `"McDonald"` and `"O'Brien"` survive intact instead of becoming `"Mcdonald"`.
- **Particles** like `de`, `van`, `bin` are lowercased unless they begin the name.
- If you'd rather have a stricter rule (e.g. always uppercase everything, or reject names containing digits), the `case` parameter and `_ILLEGAL` regex are the two places to adjust.

## Assumptions

"Normalized" is ambiguous, so I picked a concrete, defensible definition:

- Unicode-normalized (NFC), whitespace collapsed, soft hyphens/zero-width chars removed
- Title-cased per word, with **hyphens** and **apostrophes** treated as word boundaries (`jean-luc` → `Jean-Luc`, `o'neil` → `O'Neil`)
- **Name particles** kept lowercase (`van`, `de`, `di`, `la`, …) unless they're the only word of the surname
- **Mc/Mac** prefixes handled (`mcdonald` → `McDonald`)
- **Suffixes** canonicalized (`jr` → `Jr.`, `phd` → `PhD`)
- Empty/`None` inputs tolerated; output is always `First Last` (or another style on request)

```python
"""Helpers for producing a normalized display name."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata

__all__ = ["normalize_display_name"]

# Lowercase particles that belong to the name rather than to a title.
_PARTICLES = frozenset({
    "al", "bin", "da", "das", "de", "del", "der", "di", "dos", "du",
    "la", "le", "van", "von", "y",
})

# Canonical spellings for generational/academic suffixes.
_SUFFIXES = {
    "jr": "Jr.", "sr": "Sr.", "ii": "II", "iii": "III", "iv": "IV",
    "phd": "PhD", "md": "MD", "esq": "Esq.",
}

_APOSTROPHES = "'’ʼ"
_SPLIT_RE = re.compile(r"([-" + _APOSTROPHES + r"])")
_WS_RE = re.compile(r"\s+")
_INVISIBLE = dict.fromkeys(map(ord, "­​‌‍﻿"), None)


def _clean(value: str | None) -> str:
    """Normalize unicode + whitespace; treat None as empty."""
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError(f"expected str or None, got {type(value).__name__}")
    value = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", value)
    value = value.translate(_INVISIBLE)
    value = value.replace(" ", " ")          # non-breaking space
    return _WS_RE.sub(" ", value).strip()


def _title_word(word: str) -> str:
    """Title-case a single word, respecting hyphens and apostrophes."""
    if not word:
        return word
    low = word.lower()
    if low.startswith("mac") and len(word) > 3:
        return "Mac" + word[3:].capitalize()
    if low.startswith("mc") and len(word) > 2:
        return "Mc" + word[2:].capitalize()

    out, cap_next = [], True
    for part in _SPLIT_RE.split(word):
        if part == "-" or part in _APOSTROPHES:
            out.append(part)
            cap_next = True
        else:
            out.append(part.capitalize() if cap_next else part.lower())
            cap_next = False
    return "".join(out)


def _fmt_given(tokens: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Format given-name tokens (particles lowercase after the first)."""
    out = []
    for i, tok in enumerate(tokens):
        if i > 0 and tok.lower().rstrip(".") in _PARTICLES:
            out.append(tok.lower())
        else:
            out.append(_title_word(tok))
    return out


def _fmt_family(tokens: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Format surname tokens (suffixes canonicalized, particles lowercase)."""
    out = []
    for tok in tokens:
        key = tok.lower().rstrip(".")
        if key in _SUFFIXES:
            out.append(_SUFFIXES[key])
        elif len(tokens) > 1 and key in _PARTICLES:
            out.append(tok.lower())
        else:
            out.append(_title_word(tok))
    return out


def normalize_display_name(
    first: str | None,
    last: str | None,
    *,
    style: str = "first_last",
    case: str = "title",
) -> str:
    """Return a normalized display name built from ``first`` and ``last``.

    Args:
        first: Given name (may be empty/None).
        last: Family name (may be empty/None).
        style: ``"first_last"`` (default), ``"last_first"`` (``"Smith, Jane"``),
            or ``"f_last"`` (``"J. Smith"``).
        case: ``"title"`` (default), ``"upper"``, ``"lower"``, or ``"preserve"``
            (whitespace/unicode cleanup only).

    Returns:
        The normalized display name; ``""`` if both inputs are empty.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If an input is not a string or None.
        ValueError: If ``style`` or ``case`` is not a supported value.
    """
    if style not in {"first_last", "last_first", "f_last"}:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported style: {style!r}")
    if case not in {"title", "upper", "lower", "preserve"}:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported case: {case!r}")

    given_tokens = _clean(first).split(" ") if _clean(first) else []
    family_tokens = _clean(last).split(" ") if _clean(last) else []

    if case == "title":
        given, family = _fmt_given(given_tokens), _fmt_family(family_tokens)
    elif case == "preserve":
        given, family = given_tokens, family_tokens
    else:
        fn = str.upper if case == "upper" else str.lower
        given, family = [fn(t) for t in given_tokens], [fn(t) for t in family_tokens]

    given_str = " ".join(given)
    family_str = " ".join(family)

    if style == "first_last":
        return " ".join(p for p in (given_str, family_str) if p)
    if style == "last_first":
        if not family_str:
            return given_str
        return f"{family_str}, {given_str}" if given_str else family_str
    # style == "f_last"
    initials = " ".join(f"{tok[0]}." for tok in given if tok)
    return " ".join(p for p in (initials, family_str) if p)
```

## Examples

```python
normalize_display_name("  jean-luc  ", "picard")        # 'Jean-Luc Picard'
normalize_display_name("juan", "DE LA CRUZ")            # 'Juan de la Cruz'
normalize_display_name("mary", "mcdonald")              # 'Mary McDonald'
normalize_display_name("o'neil", "smith")               # "O'Neil Smith"
normalize_display_name("ludwig", "van beethoven")       # 'Ludwig van Beethoven'
normalize_display_name("elizabeth", "ii")               # 'Elizabeth II'
normalize_display_name("", "cher")                      # 'Cher'
normalize_display_name(None, None)                      # ''
normalize_display_name("jane", "smith", style="last_first")  # 'Smith, Jane'
normalize_display_name("jean luc", "picard", style="f_last") # 'J. L. Picard'
normalize_display_name("jane", "smith", case="upper")    # 'JANE SMITH'
```

## Notes / possible adjustments

- The particle and suffix lists are English/Western-centric; add entries (e.g. `"abu"`, `"el"`) or replace them entirely for other naming conventions.
- `case="preserve"` is the right choice if you're normalizing for **matching/deduplication** rather than display — it avoids destroying distinctions like `MacDonald` vs `Macdonald`.
- If you only need whitespace cleanup, the whole thing collapses to:
  ```python
  def normalize_display_name(first, last):
      return " ".join(" ".join((first or "", last or "")).split())
  ```
- If you need *sorting* keys rather than display names, a separate `sort_key()` returning `(last.lower(), first.lower())` is usually better than reusing the display string.

```python
import re


def normalized_display_name(first_name: str, last_name: str) -> str:
    """Return a normalized display name in 'First Last' form.

    Normalization rules:
      - Strip leading/trailing whitespace and collapse internal whitespace.
      - Capitalize each name (hyphens and apostrophes stay internal, so
        "mary-jane" -> "Mary-Jane" and "o'brien" -> "O'Brien").
```

## Implementation

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import os
import time
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, urlencode, urlsplit, urlunsplit


def _canonical_url(url: str) -> str:
    """Normalize a URL so equivalent URLs produce the same signature."""
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    scheme = parts.scheme.lower()
    host = (parts.hostname or "").lower()

    # Drop the port if it's the default for the scheme
    port = parts.port
    default_port = (scheme == "http" and port == 80) or (scheme == "https" and port == 443)
    netloc = host if port is None or default_port else f"{host}:{port}"

    path = parts.path or "/"
    query = urlencode(sorted(parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)))
    return urlunsplit((scheme, netloc, path, query, ""))


def build_request_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str | bytes,
    *,
    body: str | bytes = b"",
    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    timestamp: int | float | None = None,
    nonce: str | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Build an HMAC-SHA256 signature for an HTTP request.

    Returns a dict with:
      - "headers":      headers to attach to the outgoing request
      - "signature":   the hex signature
      - "canonical":   the exact string that was signed (useful for debugging)
    """
    key = api_key.encode() if isinstance(api_key, str) else api_key
    method = method.upper()
    ts = str(int(timestamp if timestamp is not None else time.time()))
    nonce = nonce or os.urandom(8).hex()

    body_bytes = body.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body, str) else (body or b"")
    body_hash = hashlib.sha256(body_bytes).hexdigest()

    # Canonicalize any extra headers (lowercase name, trimmed value, sorted)
    canonical_headers = ""
    if headers:
        items = sorted(
            (k.lower(), " ".join(str(v).split())) for k, v in headers.items()
        )
        canonical_headers = "\n".join(f"{k}:{v}" for k, v in items)

    canonical = "\n".join(
        [
            method,
            _canonical_url(url),
            ts,
            nonce,
            canonical_headers,
            body_hash,
        ]
    )

    signature = hmac.new(key, canonical.encode("utf-8"), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

    return {
        "headers": {
            "X-Timestamp": ts,
            "X-Nonce": nonce,
            "X-Signature": signature,
        },
        "signature": signature,
        "canonical": canonical,
    }
```

## Usage

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.example.com/v1/orders?page=2"
method = "POST"
api_key = "s3cr3t-key"
payload = {"item": "widget", "qty": 3}

sig = build_request_signature(
    url,
    method,
    api_key,
    body=payload,
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
)

resp = requests.request(
    method,
    url,
    json=payload,
    headers={**sig["headers"], "Content-Type": "application/json"},
)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

## Notes

- **The key is never transmitted** — it only signs the request. If your API expects a key *ID* alongside the signature, add it as a separate header (e.g. `X-Key-Id`).
- **Sign exactly what you send.** The body hash and canonical headers must match the bytes on the wire, so compute the signature *after* serializing the body.
- **Timestamp + nonce** provide replay protection; the server should reject requests with an old timestamp or a repeated nonce.
- **Use `hmac.new` / `hashlib.sha256`**, not a hand-rolled hash — `hmac.compare_digest` should be used on the server side to compare signatures in constant time.
- This is a generic scheme; if you're integrating with a real provider (AWS SigV4, Stripe, GitHub, etc.), follow that provider's exact canonicalization rules instead.

Below is a self-contained implementation of a small, AWS‑SigV4‑style request signature (HMAC‑SHA256 over a canonical request). It's a simplified scheme — not a published standard — but it has the right shape: canonicalize → hash → sign → attach headers.

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, parse_qsl, quote

ALGORITHM = "HMAC-SHA256"


def _sha256_hex(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _canonical_query(query: str) -> str:
    """Sort query params and percent-encode them consistently."""
    params = sorted(parse_qsl(query, keep_blank_values=True))
    return "&".join(f"{quote(k, safe='')}={quote(v, safe='')}" for k, v in params)


def sign_request(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    *,
    body: bytes | str = b"",
    timestamp: str | None = None,
    extra_headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Build the headers needed to authenticate an HTTP request.

    Args:
        url: Full request URL (scheme, host, path, optional query).
        method: HTTP verb, e.g. "GET" or "POST".
        api_key: Shared secret used as the HMAC key.
        body: Request body; hashed into the signature.
        timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC stamp; defaults to now.
        extra_headers: Additional headers to include in the signature.

    Returns:
        A dict of headers to merge into the outgoing request.
    """
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    method = method.upper()
    ts = timestamp or datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    payload = body.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(body, str) else (body or b"")

    # 1. Canonical headers
    headers = {
        "host": parts.netloc,
        "x-api-date": ts,
        "content-type": "application/octet-stream",
    }
    if extra_headers:
        headers.update({k.lower(): str(v) for k, v in extra_headers.items()})
    canonical_headers = "".join(
        f"{k}:{headers[k].strip()}\n" for k in sorted(headers)
    )
    signed_headers = ";".join(sorted(headers))

    # 2. Canonical request
    canonical_request = "\n".join(
        [
            method,
            parts.path or "/",
            _canonical_query(parts.query),
            canonical_headers,
            signed_headers,
            _sha256_hex(payload),
        ]
    )

    # 3. String to sign
    scope = f"{ts[:8]}/{parts.netloc}/request"
    string_to_sign = "\n".join(
        [ALGORITHM, ts, scope, _sha256_hex(canonical_request.encode("utf-8"))]
    )

    # 4. Sign
    signature = hmac.new(
        api_key.encode("utf-8"),
        string_to_sign.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return {
        "Authorization": f"{ALGORITHM} Signature={signature}",
        "X-Api-Date": ts,
        "Content-Type": headers["content-type"],
        "X-Signed-Headers": signed_headers,
    }
```

### Example

```python
import requests

headers = sign_request(
    "https://api.example.com/v1/items?page=2&sort=name",
    "GET",
    "s3cr3t-key",
    extra_headers={"x-request-id": "abc-123"},
)

resp = requests.get("https://api.example.com/v1/items?page=2&sort=name", headers=headers)
print(resp.status_code)
```

### Server-side verification

```python
def verify(url, method, api_key, headers, body=b""):
    expected = sign_request(url, method, api_key, body=body,
                            timestamp=headers["X-Api-Date"])
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected["Authorization"], headers["Authorization"])
```

### Notes

- **Never log the API key** — it's the HMAC secret, and anyone with it can forge signatures.
- **Use `hmac.compare_digest`** (as above) rather than `==` when comparing signatures, to avoid timing leaks.
- **Replay protection:** the timestamp is part of the signed data, so the server should reject requests whose `X-Api-Date` is outside a small window (e.g. ±5 minutes).
- **Query ordering doesn't matter** — params are sorted before hashing, so `?a=1&b=2` and `?b=2&a=1` produce the same signature.
- If you need to interoperate with a real provider, use their actual scheme (AWS SigV4, Stripe, etc.) rather than this one.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Optional
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, urlencode, urlsplit


def build_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    body: bytes = b"",
    timestamp: Optional[str] = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Build a request signature and the headers needed to send it.

    The signature is HMAC-SHA256(api_key, canonical_request), where the
    canonical request is:

        METHOD \n PATH \n SORTED_QUERY \n TIMESTAMP \n SHA256(body)

    Returns a dict of headers to attach to the outgoing request.
    """
    if not api_key:
        raise ValueError("api_key must not be empty")

    parts = urlsplit(url)
    path = parts.path or "/"
    query = urlencode(sorted(parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True)))
    method = method.upper()
    timestamp = timestamp or datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    body_hash = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()

    canonical_request = "\n".join([method, path, query, timestamp, body_hash])

    signature = hmac.new(
        api_key.encode("utf-8"),
        canonical_request.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return {
        "X-Api-Key": api_key,
        "X-Timestamp": timestamp,
        "X-Content-SHA256": body_hash,
        "Authorization": f"HMAC-SHA256 {signature}",
    }
```

```python
    string_to_sign = "HMAC-SHA256\\n<ts>\\n<sha256(canonical_request)>".
```

This is a generic HMAC‑SHA256 signing scheme (similar in shape to AWS SigV4). It is **not** compatible with any specific provider's spec — if you're targeting a real API, use that provider's canonicalization rules instead.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import time
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, quote, urlsplit


def _encode(value: str) -> str:
    """RFC 3986 percent-encoding of a single path/query component."""
    return quote(str(value), safe="-_.~")


def _canonical_path(path: str) -> str:
    if not path:
        return "/"
    canonical = "/".join(_encode(seg) for seg in path.split("/"))
    return canonical or "/"


def _canonical_query(query: str) -> str:
    if not query:
        return ""
    pairs = parse_qsl(query, keep_blank_values=True)
    encoded = sorted((_encode(k), _encode(v)) for k, v in pairs)
    return "&".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in encoded)


def build_request_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    body: bytes = b"",
    headers: dict | None = None,
    timestamp: int | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Build signature headers for an HTTP request.

    Args:
        url: Full request URL (scheme, host, path, query).
        method: HTTP method, e.g. "GET" or "POST".
        api_key: Shared secret used as the HMAC key.
        body: Request body bytes (hashed into the signature).
        headers: Extra headers to include in the signature.
        timestamp: Unix seconds; defaults to now.

    Returns:
        Dict of headers to merge into the outgoing request, plus the
        intermediate "CanonicalRequest" / "StringToSign" for debugging.
    """
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    method = method.upper()
    timestamp = int(time.time() if timestamp is None else timestamp)
    date = time.strftime("%Y%m%d", time.gmtime(timestamp))

    payload_hash = hashlib.sha256(body or b"").hexdigest()

    # --- Canonical headers -------------------------------------------------
    to_sign = {k.lower(): " ".join(str(v).split()) for k, v in (headers or {}).items()}
    to_sign.setdefault("host", parts.netloc)
    to_sign["x-timestamp"] = str(timestamp)
    to_sign["x-content-sha256"] = payload_hash

    signed_headers = ";".join(sorted(to_sign))
    canonical_headers = "".join(f"{k}:{to_sign[k]}\n" for k in sorted(to_sign))

    # --- Canonical request -------------------------------------------------
    canonical_request = "\n".join([
        method,
        _canonical_path(parts.path),
        _canonical_query(parts.query),
        canonical_headers,
        signed_headers,
        payload_hash,
    ])

    # --- String to sign ----------------------------------------------------
    scope = f"{date}/{parts.netloc}/request"
    string_to_sign = "\n".join([
        "HMAC-SHA256",
        str(timestamp),
        scope,
        hashlib.sha256(canonical_request.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
    ])

    # --- Derive key and sign ------------------------------------------------
    signing_key = hmac.new(api_key.encode("utf-8"), date.encode("utf-8"), hashlib.sha256).digest()
    signature = hmac.new(
        signing_key, string_to_sign.encode("utf-8"), hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()

    return {
        "Authorization": (
            f"HMAC-SHA256 Credential={api_key}, "
            f"SignedHeaders={signed_headers}, Signature={signature}"
        ),
        "X-Timestamp": str(timestamp),
        "X-Signature": signature,
        "SignedHeaders": signed_headers,
        "CanonicalRequest": canonical_request,
        "StringToSign": string_to_sign,
    }
```

## Usage

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.example.com/v1/items?b=2&a=1"
sig = build_request_signature(url, "GET", "s3cr3t-key")

resp = requests.get(
    url,
    headers={k: v for k, v in sig.items() if k in ("Authorization", "X-Timestamp")},
)
```

## Notes

- **Determinism:** the same `(url, method, key, body, headers, timestamp)` always yields the same signature — pass an explicit `timestamp` in tests.
- **Key separation:** the signing key is derived per-day (`HMAC(key, date)`), so rotating the secret invalidates old signatures immediately.

- **Body hashing:** `x-content-sha256` binds the payload; if you sign a body, send those exact bytes.
- **Query/path encoding:** paths are normalized segment-by-segment and query params are sorted, so `?a=1&b=2` and `?b=2&a=1` sign identically.

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import time
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, urlunsplit


def build_request_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    secret_key: str | None = None,
    timestamp: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """
    Build a signed set of HTTP headers for an API request.

    The signature is computed over a canonical string:
        METHOD\nnormalized_url\napi_key\ntimestamp

    Args:
        url:        The full request URL.
        method:     HTTP method (e.g. "GET", "POST").
        api_key:    The public API key / identifier.
        secret_key: The shared secret used to sign. Defaults to api_key
                    if not supplied (fine for simple examples, not for production).
        timestamp:  Unix timestamp in seconds. Defaults to now.

    Returns:
        A dict of headers to attach to the request.
    """
    if not url or not method or not api_key:
        raise ValueError("url, method, and api_key are required")

    secret = secret_key if secret_key is not None else api_key
    ts = int(time.time()) if timestamp is None else int(timestamp)

    # Normalize the URL so trivial variations (trailing slash, default port,
    # empty query) don't change the signature.
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    netloc = parts.netloc.lower()
    if (parts.scheme == "http" and netloc.endswith(":80")) or \
       (parts.scheme == "https" and netloc.endswith(":443")):
        netloc = netloc.rsplit(":", 1)[0]
    path = parts.path or "/"
    normalized_url = urlunsplit((parts.scheme.lower(), netloc, path, parts.query, ""))

    canonical = "\n".join([
        method.upper(),
        normalized_url,
        api_key,
        str(ts),
    ])

    signature = hmac.new(
        secret.encode("utf-8"),
        canonical.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()

    return {
        "X-Api-Key": api_key,
        "X-Timestamp": str(ts),
        "X-Signature": signature,
        "Authorization": f"HMAC-SHA256 {signature}",
    }
```

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, parse_qsl, quote


def _sha256_hex(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def _hmac(key: bytes, msg: str) -> bytes:
    return hmac.new(key, msg.encode("utf-8"), hashlib.sha256).digest()


def build_request_signature(
    url: str,
    method: str,
    api_key: str,
    secret_key: str | None = None,
    *,
    body: bytes = b"",
    region: str = "us-east-1",
    service: str = "api",
    timestamp: datetime | None = None,
    extra_headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Build the headers needed to sign an HTTP request.

    Args:
        url: Full request URL (scheme, host, path, optional query string).
        method: HTTP verb, e.g. "GET" or "POST".
        api_key: Key identifier; appears in the Authorization credential scope.
        secret_key: Signing secret. Defaults to `api_key` if omitted.
        body: Raw request body bytes (hashed into the signature).
        region/service: Scope components for the credential string.
        timestamp: Signing time; defaults to now (UTC).
        extra_headers: Additional headers to include in the signature.

    Returns:
        A dict of headers to merge into the outgoing request.
    """
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    method = method.upper()
    secret_key = secret_key if secret_key is not None else api_key

    ts = timestamp or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    amz_date = ts.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    date_stamp = ts.strftime("%Y%m%d")

    # --- Canonical request -------------------------------------------------
    canonical_uri = quote(parts.path or "/", safe="/-_.~")
    canonical_query = "&".join(
        f"{quote(k, safe='-_.~')}={quote(v, safe='-_.~')}"
        for k, v in sorted(parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True))
    )

    headers = {"host": parts.netloc, "x-amz-date": amz_date}
    if extra_headers:
        headers.update({k.lower(): str(v) for k, v in extra_headers.items()})
    if body and "content-type" not in headers:
        headers["content-type"] = "application/octet-stream"

    canonical_headers = "".join(
        f"{k}:{' '.join(str(v).split())}\n" for k, v in sorted(headers.items())
    )
    signed_headers = ";".join(sorted(headers))
    hashed_payload = _sha256_hex(body)

    canonical_request = "\n".join(
        [
            method,
            canonical_uri,
            canonical_query,
            canonical_headers,
            signed_headers,
            hashed_payload,
        ]
    )

    # --- String to sign ----------------------------------------------------
    scope = f"{date_stamp}/{region}/{service}/aws4_request"
    string_to_sign = "\n".join(
        [
            "AWS4-HMAC-SHA256",
            amz_date,
            scope,
            _sha256_hex(canonical_request.encode("utf-8")),
        ]
    )

    # --- Derive the signing key --------------------------------------------
    k_date = _hmac(("AWS4" + secret_key).encode("utf-8"), date_stamp)
    k_region = _hmac(k_date, region)
    k_service = _hmac(k_region, service)
    k_signing = _hmac(k_service, "aws4_request")

    signature = hmac.new(
        k_signing, string_to_sign.encode("utf-8"), hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()

    headers["authorization"] = (
        f"AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential={api_key}/{scope}, "
        f"SignedHeaders={signed_headers}, Signature={signature}"
    )
    return headers
```
